I really don't like leaving a bad review for games seemingly everyone likes, but I've tried countless times to enjoy this game and I simply can't do it. Even alcohol was no help in enjoying this game. It's unbearably dull, and frankly I think an actual sedative pill would be both cheaper and more effective than playing this game.

The game punishes me if I work too much by taking my money, time, and stamina, but then makes every other option equally as monotonous as farming with none of the charm. It somehow makes relaxing hobbies like fishing mind-numbing and obnoxious, and exciting hobbies like adventuring tedious and boring. Everything important other than seeds is worth the price of a small house, and an astoundingly large portion of the game was interrupted by waiting on my phone for stores to open. I even considered that the game wanted to be played as a visual novel and started to focus on talking to characters, only to find that the mayor is the only one willing to give me more than two unique dialogues and the cutscenes almost put me to sleep several times. On top of that, I got a cat that glitched into my bed and prevented me from ending the day the same day I got him, and the game crashed two separate times in one sitting. The farthest I could bring myself to play was day 20 singleplayer.

Playing with friends has always been people who enjoy the game going crazy doing everything in a few days or so and then throwing me at endgame mechanics they think I would enjoy without telling me anything or even letting me do anything at all. I usually built a small garden that was summarily taken down because I was doing it wrong, and was essentially sitting in my bed on my phone for hours while my friends played the game. Perhaps this is my fault, and I may be generalizing here, but I don't see a reason why playing with randoms would be any better, and I'm not subjecting myself to this game again just to find out. At any rate, the farthest I could bring myself to play was day 5-6 multiplayer.

Clearly there's a way to enjoy this game, since everyone I've ever met has loved this game, but the only enjoyment I've ever gotten out of it each time I've played has been listening to the soundtrack, which, hilariously, makes an hour of Spotify and the sedative pill a better experience than this game has been for me.

Quite the paradox given I have put over 130 hours into this game. It started out fun from what I saw in the trailers and gameplay. But the more I played the more I could tell this game was a great idea for me, it just didn't pan out in the grooling end. I pushed myself to give this game a chance which turned into a chore rather than fun.

Major flaw is that Stardew Valley wants to be a slow burn game, which it is. It's just the wick had already run it's course when you start to see the gameplay loop and the insufferable, unnecessary grind. Which leads me to believe the greatest villain in the game is not the monsters in the mine that you savagely brutalize for your own gain. It's Stardew Valley itself. It wants to consume your free time much like social media corporations.

There's 0.01% drop rates for certain items that you can only find in certain seasons, in specific weather conditions, at just the right time of day and if you miss it that's it. And this is a single player game. I propose being more creative with a situation such as this. Adding special story behind why this is such a rare thing, including unique game play tailored to finding it or coming across it in the wild building up intrigue, mystique, and maybe even tension if it's horror related.

Instead you have to pass all these mediocre checks and balances, go to point A, grind forever and ever doing the same monotonous activity hoping machine generated luck is on your side this time. Head to point B to sleep because you have a stamina system. Rinse, repeat.

But I am glad others are enjoying it! It just wasn't for me.

Game rushes you to do literally everything, time passes extremely fast and NPCs have extremely annoying "realistic" schedules that only serve to make the game artificially more difficult with it's stupid time management system.

Quests from outside Pierre's and the bulletin board give you barely enough time to complete them if you don't already have the needed items, because NPCs all have schedules and all lock their doors at 6pm (some even sooner), even though days go until 2am. 
Speaking of which, you instantly fall unconscious at 2am and lose ten percent of your money. Early-midgame this can be devastating. There are TONS of "OH CRAP" moments where you look at the time and start rushing back from the beach or somewhere far away only to pass out on your farm and lose a ton of money. It is extremely unforgiving, doesn't matter how much energy you have you WILL fall unconscious at 2am.
Want to go fishing and level up your skill? Gotta water all your plants first and take care of your animals. Oh, now it's hours later and you barely have enough time to catch 4 fish before you need to RUSH back or pass out and lose ten percent of your money.

There was a time when I got a quest to collect and deliver 100 bone fragments to the museum within 6 days.
6 days. Meanwhile I have to water all my plants and also take care of the animals. Oh, and you can only get bone fragments from very specific levels of the mine from specific enemies that only drop 0-1 per kill. ZERO to ONE. I worked SUPER hard to get all these bone fragments and actually had to let myself pass out in the mines a few times to do it, only to get right next to the museum doors and have them close on me as it turned 6pm on the 6th and final day, failing the quest. Ridiculous.

If you enjoy feeling rushed, feeling anxious, not ever having enough time to do everything you want, NPCs having extremely irritating "realistic" schedules where you'll fail a quest because today is Robin's "lock my door at 2pm and watch tv all day" day, then you'll like this game.
Great farming sim similar to Harvest Moon, but the time management system and the "realistic NPC schedules" system is absolutely atrocious and not at all enjoyable.
Oh, and there's also no point in doing anything other than planting and selling crops. Mining, fishing and the other things you can do and get proficient in only make a small percentage of what selling crops do.

Stardew Valley... what a colossal waste of time! This game is like a black hole sucking away any semblance of productivity from your life.

First off, the graphics are reminiscent of something from the stone age. Are we supposed to be impressed by these pixelated blobs pretending to be characters? It's like playing a game from the 1980s, but without the charm. And don't even get me started on the animation. It's so stiff and lifeless; I've seen more lively animations in a PowerPoint presentation.

The gameplay? Oh, where do I begin? It's a mind-numbing loop of planting crops, watering crops, and waiting... and waiting... and waiting. Congratulations, you've just spent your precious real-life hours pretending to be a virtual farmer. And don't even think about escaping to the mines for some excitement. It's just mindless clicking and swinging your pickaxe at the same old rocks.

The characters in this game are about as interesting as watching paint dry. They spout off the same tired lines day after day, and good luck trying to form any meaningful relationships with them. It's like trying to bond with cardboard cutouts. And let's not forget about the so-called "romance" options. They're as shallow as a puddle in a desert.

And the music... ugh! It's like a never-ending loop of elevator music that drills into your skull. It's like the game developers wanted to punish you for even daring to play their game.

In conclusion, Stardew Valley is a soul-sucking abyss that will devour your time and leave you feeling emptier than when you started. Do yourself a favor and steer clear of this digital monstrosity. You'll thank me later.

I bought this game impulsively during my freshman year of college when I was going through a lot at the time and honestly- BEST. DECISION. EVER. 

Not only does this game help me cope with my struggles in life, but it's also incredibly addicting and so much fun to play with. During my first playthrough, I spent around 140 hours in total and still haven't fully reached 100% of the game because the grinding aspect does take quite some time. I didn't mind the grinding aspect of it because it felt rewarding to see how much your farm has changed over the few years I played through and grinding was also pretty fun for me (especially with all the sound effects when you cut trees or smash rocks). 

And now, I'm on my second playthrough (to try out the 1.6 patch update) and it's as if I'm playing the game as a new player because there are many ways with how you want to play and/or progress through with the game. I first fell in love with Sebastian in my first playthrough and even had two kids with him, so I decided to romance Elliott on my second and I love him just as much as I love Sebastian. If possible, I might even create different game files to romance other bachelors/bachelorettes because I don't want to divorce them :') I'd rather start all over again because I think it's fun that way.

Stardew Valley also definitely deserves the hype it gets, especially as it is created by a solo developer. I think that's such an inspiration and I see it as a motivational force since I am currently studying to be a game developer. I also wish that i can create a game that many people would love.

So, if you're ever looking for a chill yet also challenging game to play during your spare time, then you should definitely try this game out!
